mappings.note: The Khyber Pass as the route used by armies, scholars and caravans alike. CG-SST1 for the corridor as a geographical fact, LO-55 for its military use; LO-48 is rejected because the question never asks how the pass formed.
Why Mahmud plundered temples - wealth and religious assertion. A ruler's campaign motive, LO-55; LO-56 is reserved for items that set his motive against Ghuri's.
Al-Biruni learning Sanskrit and comparing Indian and Greek science. Cross-cultural transmission of knowledge, goal-level CG-SST2.
Bhaskaracharya's Lilavati, Bijaganita and Siddhantashiromani. History of science, goal-level CG-SST2.
Sena cultural influence in Bengal, resting on their patronage of Jayadeva and the Gitagovindam. LO-59 for the devotional poetry, LO-55 for the dynasty's patronage as policy.
Eastern Ganga building at Puri and Konark. Temple construction, LO-57.
The legend of Sala striking the tiger behind the Hoysala name. Dynastic origin story, LO-55.
What sets Hoysala temples apart - carved pillars, sculpture and panels at Belur and Halebidu. Distinctive style and technique, LO-57 exactly.
Rajaraja's overseas conquests in the Maldives and northern Sri Lanka. Military expansion, LO-55.

Mapped on its stem, which asks why Rajendra Chola I attacked Srivijaya - a naval strategy question, LO-55. (The options and answer stored here belong to the vihara question; the two rows are transposed. See report.)

The Kakatiya fort at Warangal and its stone toranas. Monumental construction and its distinctive gateways, LO-57; LO-55 is not added because the fort is identified by its craftsmanship, not its defensive role.

An agrarian economy with thriving cash crops, against the false claim that maritime trade had stopped. Economic history of the period, goal-level CG-SST2. (Stem survives only as its last line; see report.)
Locating Srivijaya in present-day Malaysia and Indonesia, astride the Malacca Strait. Location on a world map; goal-level CG-SST1, LO-50 being climatic regions only.
Amoghavarsha I's title Nripatunga, 'peak of kings'. Royal titulature, LO-55.
Chahamanas rising in Rajasthan before taking Delhi, Haryana and Punjab. Territorial expansion, LO-55.
The Khyber Pass as the choke point the Hindu Shahis held. LO-55 for holding a pass as defence policy, CG-SST1 for the geography that makes it one.
Mahmud of Ghazni defeating Jayapala. Military outcome, LO-55.
Mahmud taking the title 'sultan'. Titulature and claim to sovereignty, LO-55.
Somanatha as the Saurashtra temple Mahmud destroyed. The raid is what is recalled, LO-55, matching the 1026 item.
Al-Biruni as the scholar in Mahmud's train. A source and its author, goal-level CG-SST2.
Lilavati as Bhaskaracharya's riddle-based mathematical text. History of science, goal-level CG-SST2.
Nadiya as the Sena capital Bakhtiyar Khilji took. Campaign and its target, LO-55.
Eastern Gangas as builders of Konark. Temple construction by dynasty, LO-57.
Orugallu (Warangal) as the Kakatiya capital. Seat of a kingdom, LO-55; the fort item carries LO-57 instead, which is the distinction.
Hoysalas as builders at Belur and Halebidu. Temple construction, LO-57.
Rajaraja Chola as builder of the Brihadishvara. Temple construction, LO-57.
Srivijaya as the empire Rajendra Chola I defeated. Military expansion overseas, LO-55.

Someshvara III as author of the Manasollasa. Bare authorship recall, so a source-identification item, goal-level CG-SST2; the longer Manasollasa item also carries LO-55 because it states the text's subject is governance.
Vishishtadvaita vedanta as Ramanuja's school. A new religious-philosophical position, LO-58.
Basaveshvara as founder of the Lingayats. Emergence of a religious movement, LO-58.
Angkor Wat as the world's largest religious monument. Monument identification, LO-57.
King Bhoja building the great lake near Bhopal. A ruler's public work, LO-55; the water-management framing is picked up separately by the Malwa irrigation item.
The Samarangana Sutradhara as Bhoja's treatise on architecture and mechanical devices. A text on building, LO-57.
The Second Battle of Tarain as the 1192 defeat of Prithviraja III. Military outcome, LO-55.
Mularaja II as the Chaulukya who beat Ghuri at Mount Abu. Military outcome, LO-55. (The stored answer runs on into stray option text; see report.)

This row's stem is two questions run together; the scored content is what its answer resolves - Bakhtiyar Khilji's disastrous 1205 push towards Tibet, broken in Kamarupa. A failed campaign, LO-55. (Merged stem; see report.)

Assertion-reason rejecting the claim that destroying Nalanda and Vikramashila mattered little. LO-55 for the campaign; C-SST2.3 at competency level for its effect on the religious landscape, since LO-58 covers the emergence of movements and not their decline.
Patanjali's Yogasutras as the text al-Biruni rendered into Arabic. Transmission of texts, goal-level CG-SST2.
A king consulting a treatise on architecture, mechanical devices and water management, resolved to Bhoja's Samarangana Sutradhara. Building knowledge, LO-57.
Chahamana inscriptions naming the city Dhillika, later Delhi. A kingdom's city as its own records name it, LO-55.
Vijayabahu I expelling the Cholas from northern Sri Lanka after half a century. Military outcome, LO-55.
Lakshmi on Ghuri's gold coin, continuing a motif used since the Kushanas. Coinage as legitimation, LO-55.

Mapped on its stem, which asks what a vihara is - a Buddhist monastery that served as a college, as in Nalanda Mahavihara. Historical terminology and institutions, goal-level CG-SST2. (The answer stored here belongs to the Rajendra Chola question; the two rows are transposed. See report.)
Why Rajendra Chola took the title Gangaikondachola after his northern campaign. Titulature commemorating conquest, LO-55.
Chola decline through drawn-out wars with the Pandyas and Western Chalukyas draining the treasury. The cost of a military strategy, LO-55.

Bhoja damming rivers into a vast lake for Malwa's irrigation. LO-55 for a ruler's public works, LO-54 for water conservation - the answer makes irrigation the purpose, which the bare 'who built the lake' item does not.
The Samarangana Sutradhara's focus on architecture, town planning, temples and machines. Building knowledge, LO-57.
Ghuri's aim of permanent conquest set against Mahmud's plunder. A direct LO-56 fit, comparing two rulers' policies.
The Second Battle of Tarain's result and the fall of Delhi. Military outcome, LO-55.

Bakhtiyar Khilji's eastern campaigns and the decline of Indian Buddhism that followed. LO-55 for the campaign, C-SST2.3 at competency level for the religious consequence, LO-58 covering emergence rather than decline.
Why the Tibet expedition failed - Kamarupa's forces destroying food and fodder. Military strategy and counter-strategy, LO-55.
How rulers funded large armies - tribute from vassals and taxes on agriculture and trade. Administrative measures underwriting military control, a direct LO-55 fit.
Agriculture as the mainstay of the period's economy. Economic history, goal-level CG-SST2; LO-51 is rejected because no climatic region is being related to a way of life.
Basaveshvara, minister turned reformer, founding the Lingayats. Emergence of a religious movement, LO-58.
Lingayat belief: rejection of caste and ritualism for devotion, work and spiritual equality. LO-58 for the movement's tenets, LO-60 because equality is the substance of them.

Ramanuja's vishishtadvaita challenging Advaita by holding the world real. A new religious-philosophical position, LO-58. (The stored answer breaks off into an advertising line and unrelated text; see report.)
The consequences of Bakhtiyar Khilji's campaigns - the Sena collapse in Bengal and the burning of Nalanda's libraries. LO-55 for the military and political result, C-SST2.3 for the blow to Buddhism.
The Lingayat movement's significance in rejecting hierarchy and asserting spiritual equality through the anubhava mandapa. LO-58 for the movement, LO-60 for the equality claim it rests on.

Angkor Wat as evidence of Indian influence abroad - dedicated to Vishnu, carved with Hindu epics, echoing south Indian temple form. LO-57 for the architecture, CG-SST2 for the cultural transmission it demonstrates.

The economic base of the period's kingdoms: rice, spices and cotton underpinned by ruler-built irrigation. CG-SST2 for the economy, LO-55 because the answer credits the irrigation networks to the rulers' own works.
